title: Chapter 1865: Lifeless Lowlands (I)
content:
Chapter 1865: Lifeless Lowlands (I)

Brilliant colors filled the cave dwelling. Seated at its center, a man studied a formation diagram with his eyes lowered in thought. After a long while, he looked up and let out a long breath.

Liu Changdie seldom went out and led a quiet life on the island. With no further path for his cultivation, he devoted most of his attention to his Dao conduct and formation arts. His days truly were spent in secluded cultivation.

His frustration at being unable to advance had gradually faded away.

Rather than saying I've accepted my fate... I'd say reaching this point has already made this life worthwhile.

Sensing something, he counted on his fingers, and his eyes brightened. He rose and flew out of the cave dwelling to see a bank of green clouds drifting in from the west. It descended before the island, revealing an old Daoist Master.

Liu Changdie looked a little embarrassed and hurriedly lowered his head. "Greetings, senior!"

The old Daoist Master Shanbai merely nodded with a smile. He was charitable and generous, as well as a middle stage Purple Mansion Realm cultivator of Horn Wood. Cultivators generally showed him some respect, and his mountain gate stood by the sea. Despite the ongoing conflict between north and south, he had remained entirely untouched.

Shanbai seemed to recognize Liu Changdie. Bringing his hands together, he smiled. "Fate has brought us together again... You've reached the Purple Mansion Realm too, fellow Daoist! That [Four Constants Wood] went to a worthy recipient!"

Liu Changdie grew even more embarrassed. Back when his cultivation was still low, he had recalled from his memories of his previous life that a rogue cultivator had rescued an old man on an island in the Eastern Sea and received a treasure. He had waited at the spot and claimed that opportunity for himself.

Yet the treasure he received had belonged to Wood Virtue rather than [Returning Earth], as it should have. He had been puzzled at the time, but assumed the old man had simply acted on a whim.

Now, of course, he understood that Daoist Master Shanbai had descended from his mountain to bestow the treasure on a particular person. He had merely intervened. He hurriedly apologized. "You must find my behavior laughable, senior... I only hope I didn't disrupt anything important!"

Shanbai shook his head with a smile. "It was nothing important. I saw a descendant of an old acquaintance and decided to lend a hand. I intended to have the youngster take a spirit item back to him... I hoped it would help him reach the Purple Mansion Realm. But a surge of spiritual aura took his life. I don't know whether he ever used it.

"Whether you had intervened or not, it would have made no difference..."

Liu Changdie could only nod. Just as their conversation ended, clouds and rain swept in from the north. Amid flood dragons drawing a carriage attended by crabs, a woman appeared. Dressed in white Daoist robes, she was lovely and graceful.

As she alighted on the island, Liu Changdie stepped forward and bowed. "Greetings, Daoist Master!"

Daoist Nun Xiangchun returned his greeting. "I came as requested. There is no need for such courtesy, fellow Daoist."

Liu Changdie knew whose request she meant, and had long known this day would come. Before his rebirth, he had never even met Li Xuanxuan. The old man had died very, very early, seemingly during the upheaval of a devil plague!

He must have escaped some fatal calamity, then survived until now thanks to years of nourishment from spirit items... But now that Yuanjiao is gone, I ought to keep his father safe.

Liu Changdie led her to a seat in the pavilion. Having spent many years in the Eastern Sea, Shanbai was acquainted with the Daoist nun and greeted her casually.

Liu Changdie courteously had someone serve tea, then said, "The elder is not only a senior of the King of Wei's family, but also my benefactor. Thank you for coming so far, Daoist Master. If there is anything you need, please say the word. I would hardly presume to give you orders."

Xiangchun nodded. The three Daoist Masters looked up together as the great void finally stirred. Li Ximing emerged on a streak of light, greeted each of them, and said with a smile, "Thank you all for your trouble!"

Behind him, however, Li Xuanxuan stared around in astonishment, a thousand words caught in his chest.

His ailments stemmed from damage to his foundations, which could only deteriorate, never recover. There was no cure. In any other family, or even in his own a few decades earlier, he would simply have been cared for through his remaining years, waiting for death!

Yet three Daoist Masters had come. Including Li Ximing, who had brought him here, four Daoist Masters were going to such lengths for his worn-out body!

Li Xuanxuan had never considered himself anyone important. Back then, lowly cultivators had fallen like weeds in the market towns, and countless others had died young in battle. If his descendants had not done so well, sparing him from risking his life outside, and if he had not enjoyed a little luck himself... how could he still be alive today? He had already lived more than long enough.

When Li Ximing had asked him to come, Li Xuanxuan had agreed simply to put his grandson's mind at ease. Now his eyes reddened, and his heart trembled.

For this humble body of mine... Why go to such lengths...

Every Purple Mansion Realm cultivator present was keenly perceptive and naturally noticed the old man's distress. Taking a talisman from her sleeve, Daoist Master Xiangchun looked up with a touch of emotion.

"When the letter reached the Dragon Palace, Heyun read it first and made a special trip to the Thunder Pool. Only then did we learn that you are the Thunder Maiden's eldest uncle. Whether as a public duty or a personal matter, this deserves our attention."

A glimmer of hope appeared in Li Xuanxuan's eyes at her words. "I haven't seen Qinghong in so many years..."

Li Ximing turned away in silence. As her talisman fluttered, Daoist Master Xiangchun prepared her Valley Water and said softly, "The Thunder Pool involves the secrets of thunder devouring. It must be guarded, and outsiders must not be allowed to discover its true condition. Naturally, it cannot readily be left unattended."

The old man nodded repeatedly. Shanbai was already inwardly astonished to see Xiangchun explain this to him herself.

No wonder they've gone to such lengths... This is the sort of care other families would give a wounded Daoist Master. So this is the kind of old ancestor he is...

Xiangchun shifted the talisman's light, releasing a gentle flow of dark radiance that soothed the old man's emotions. She closed her eyes and formed hand seals to invoke her divine ability, while Shanbai reached out to take his pulse. Silence fell over the pavilion.

After a long while, under Liu Changdie's worried gaze, Xiangchun opened her eyes. She exchanged a glance with Shanbai and spoke first. "The elder's lifespan is indeed nearing its end. He suffered some serious injuries in his middle age that cost him a dozen or so years of life. Fortunately, he has been well cared for in his later years. The damage has not worsened, and much has been done to nourish his body. Everything possible has truly been done to sustain him until today.

"I can see a golden pellet within him. It should be a technique of the Hengzhu Dao, used to calm the mind, focus the spirit, and dispel inner demons. Hengzhu's techniques often work wonders through spirits and ghosts. It has helped him greatly over the years. Without this art, his body would likely have given out long ago."

Li Ximing nodded solemnly. The old man wiped away his tears, thinking of Li Xijun. The two visiting Daoist Masters fell silent, and Li Ximing chose his words carefully. "Grandfather, it has been a long time since you last saw Senior Liu. Why not catch up with him first?"

Li Xuanxuan nodded silently and left with Liu Changdie supporting him. Shanbai nodded, then picked up the thread. "Ever since Wood Virtue's decline in ancient times, all means of extending lifespan have been incomplete. The [Calamity of Severed Nourishment] weakened them further. Unorthodox approaches generally yield the best results, but the elder's cultivation is too low to withstand them."

Xiangchun said, "I was instructed beforehand to favor gentle care. Given his low cultivation, I won't discuss methods involving subservience or refinement. Others involve cutting bones or refining blood, which are too painful and bloody. Your family follows the Orthodox Dao, so naturally I would not propose using them.

"I think the best approach is simply to extend his lifespan. He cultivates Pristine Water, and his cultivation is low, so doing so should not be particularly difficult."
